target_customer: Startups and small companies that need design, web and no-code talent on a monthly subscription
problem: Hiring and vetting freelance designers and developers is slow and unreliable; Awesomic matches vetted talent within 24 hours on a flat subscription.
business_model: Marketplace plus managed subscription, flat monthly fee per matched talent
product_category: Talent marketplace for product and design talent, later AI plus experts workspace

founders.name: Stacy Pavlyshyna
education: Graduated from two universities at once at age 19 (schools not named on the YC page)
previous_startups: Awesomic is her third business per the YC page
founders.background_notes: About five years in marketing; Forbes 30 Under 30 per the YC page. Other sources give her title as CEO, COO or founder.

founders.name: Roman Sevast
education: Dropped out of college (school not named)
previous_startups: Earlier startups and game servers started from age 13 (not named)
founders.background_notes: Self-taught builder from Ukraine; Forbes 30 Under 30 per the YC page. Wikipedia lists him as CEO or president.

investors: angels incl. James Park and Ragnar Sass

technical_complexity.rationale: A matching marketplace and project app with vetting is mostly web product work; the hard part is supply quality, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: Vetted talent supply and process give some edge, but design subscriptions were easy for others to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Awesomic; many later comparison posts list design subscription rivals.

market_need_then: Startups needed on-demand design and no-code talent; Awesomic reports 1,000+ businesses served early 2022 and 4,000+ later (self reported, company about page).

branding.domain_note: Uses awesomic.com. Trademark AWESOMIC filed June 3, 2021 by Awesomic, Inc.

identity.logo: Wordmark with a smiling mascot icon
identity.voice_and_tone: Upbeat taglines such as Take a deep breath and Awesomic

branding.brand_signature: Awesome as a verb (Take a deep breath and Awesomic)
branding.community_and_virality: Founders appear in Forbes 30 Under 30 per the YC page; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Upbeat memorable name and founder press in Ukrainian tech media, but no evidence the brand itself drove growth.

pivots.from: Design and no-code talent marketplace on subscription
pivots.to: AI agents plus vetted human experts workspace
pivots.why: Not stated by a source; the current site and YC launch post describe the AI plus experts product.

outcome_analysis: Awesomic raised a small pre-seed, YC money, a 2 million dollar seed in December 2021 and 800 thousand dollars in March 2023, and reports serving over 4,000 companies with a team of about 150. It has stayed independent and appears to be growing modestly, with a recent move toward AI agents combined with human experts. No later priced round was found, so scale of success is limited by public data.
notes: Competitor list left empty: only 2026 comparison posts (Designjoy, Superside, Design Pickle, ManyPixels) were found, none dated near the 2021 batch. 2023 round date conflicts: one draft says 2022, tech.eu and CB Insights say March 2023. CB Insights total $2.93M over 7 rounds. YC round recorded as other because the amount is reported. Pre-seed amount described as six figures by a founder quote in ain.ua. Outcome search found no acquisition, shutdown or layoffs.
